headline: release_elbow_angle
launch_angle
knee_bend

release_elbow_angle.label: Elbow extension at release
release_elbow_angle.why: A fully extended shooting arm at release gives a straighter, more repeatable ball path.

drill.name: One-hand form shooting
drill.cue: Reach into the cookie jar: finish tall, elbow locked, wrist relaxed.

launch_angle.label: Launch angle
launch_angle.why: A ball that leaves at 45–55° drops into a bigger window of the rim.

drill.name: Arc ladder
drill.cue: Shoot up and over a tall defender's hand, not at the rim.

release_height.label: Release height (above the head)
release_height.why: A higher release is harder to contest and gives the ball a better angle into the rim.

drill.name: Wall-line release
drill.cue: Ball above the forehead before it leaves your fingers.

knee_bend.label: Knee bend at the load
knee_bend.why: Power comes from the legs. A consistent dip makes your range repeatable.

drill.name: Dip-and-rise catch shooting
drill.cue: Sit into the catch, rise in one motion.

set_point_elbow_angle.label: Elbow angle at set point
set_point_elbow_angle.why: An L-shaped set point keeps the ball in the shooting pocket and the elbow under the ball.

drill.name: Pocket-to-set holds
drill.cue: Make an L. Hold one count, then shoot.

dip_to_release.label: Dip to release
dip_to_release.why: One smooth motion from the legs to the fingertips. Long pauses leak power, rushing loses balance.

arc_height.label: Arc height (apex above release)
arc_height.why: Enough arc to drop softly, but not so much that the shot loses accuracy and power.

follow_through_hold.label: Follow-through hold
follow_through_hold.why: Holding the follow-through until the ball lands builds a repeatable finish.

drill.name: Freeze-the-finish
drill.cue: Hold the gooseneck until the ball hits the floor.

balance_drift.label: Balance drift (sideways hip movement)
balance_drift.why: Landing where you took off means the shot went straight up through your body, not sideways.

drill.name: Land-on-the-line
drill.cue: Take off and land on the same spot. Feet wide, balanced.

glossary.text: Height is a crucial factor in basketball, and it plays a significant role in determining a player's position. Centers and power forwards tend to be the tallest players on the team, while point guards and shooting guards are usually shorter.
A player's wingspan is the distance between the tips of their outstretched arms. A long wingspan can help a player block shots, steal passes, and get rebounds.
Weight is an essential factor in basketball because it affects a player's strength and ability to move on the court. A player's weight must be appropriate for their position and playing style.
A player's body fat percentage is an important measure of their fitness level. A low body fat percentage can help a player move more quickly and jump higher.

Speed is a critical factor in basketball because it affects a player's ability to move quickly on the court. A fast player can drive to the basket, get open for a shot, or steal the ball from an opponent.
Agility is the ability to change direction quickly and maintain balance while doing so. It's essential for dribbling, defending, and driving to the basket.
Strength is important in basketball because it helps players to control the ball, play defense, and battle for rebounds.
